mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decline and SPX returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in the prior month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over the prior two months indicates weakening consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline > 2.0% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 2.0% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing contraction (INDPRO below 100), a decline in industrial production over the prior month signals weakening supply chain activity, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits face headwinds.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is below 100 and declines in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior month signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of housing starts (HOUST) below 1200 and GDP growth (GDPC1) below 2.0% annualized in the prior quarter signals a weakening economy, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST < 1200 and GDPC1 growth < 2.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 1.0% in the prior month, it signals monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.0%.
